# Archgen Labs

> Archgen Labs (also written Archgen) is building an AI agent for chip physical design, from a single die to a 3D stack. Picture a coding agent, except the codebase is a chip. The company is backed by Y Combinator.

## What the agent does
- Works in physical design, inside the EDA flow a team already runs; nothing is ripped out or replaced.
- Reads the run evidence: timing reports, DRC results, congestion maps and run logs.
- Finds the root cause, patches the flow files (for example floorplan.tcl and constraints.sdc) and reruns timing, DRC and congestion.
- Keeps every fix in memory and applies what worked on one block to the next.
- Built for 2D and 3D-stacked chips. Stacked dies share timing, power and heat across tiers, while most physical design tools still treat each die as a separate flat chip.

## Proof
- Ranked #1 on the IBM macro-placement benchmarks in the HRT × Partcl macro placement challenge: https://archgen.tech/blog/posts/how-we-ranked-first-in-the-partcl.html
